findings.source_quote: Ἀλλʼ οὐχ ἕνεκα τούτου ὀργίζεται σοι ὁ Θεός, ἀλλʼ ἵνα τὸν οἶκόν σου τὸν ἁμαρτήσαντα εἰς τὸν Κύριον καὶ εἰς ὑμᾶς τοὺς γονεῖς αὐτῶν ἐπιστρέψῃς.
findings.english_quote: But God is not angry with you for this. He wants you to turn back your household[a], which has sinned against the Lord and against you[h], their parents.
findings.issue: The second sentence replaces the stated purpose of God's anger with a separate statement about what God wants. The Greek contrasts the rejected reason for his anger with its corrective purpose; the simplified text no longer explicitly connects the anger to turning the household back.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “But God is not angry with you for this. His anger is meant to make you turn back your household[a], which has sinned against the Lord and against you[h], their parents.”

findings.source_quote: ἀλλὰ φιλότεκνος ὢν οὐκ ἐνουθέτεις σου τὸν οἶκον, ἀλλὰ ἀφῆκας αὐτὸν καταφθαρῆναι δεινῶς
findings.english_quote: You loved your children, but you did not admonish your household. Instead, you let it be terribly ruined.
findings.issue: The source presents Hermas's fondness for his children as the circumstance explaining his failure to admonish them. “You loved your children, but” instead presents love and failure to admonish as contrasting facts, obscuring the source's criticism of indulgent parental affection.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “But because you were fond of your children, you did not admonish your household. Instead, you let it be terribly ruined.”

summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all four paragraphs of the selected Greek. The standard edition preserves the source's claims, conditions, negations, and contextual repentance terminology. The simplified edition needs revision to preserve two explanatory relationships in paragraph 1. Both editions' witness notes are compatible with the supplied bounded reports and distinguish editorial emendations and conjectures from reported preserved readings. This assessment does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation. Proposed replacements require fresh review.
